title: Crypto transparency: how was this password made?
intro: Prisma hides nothing. This panel shows exactly which randomness source, alphabet and math are behind the current result.
randomSourceBody: your system's cryptographically secure random generator (CSPRNG). Modulo bias is avoided via rejection sampling: random values above the largest multiple of the alphabet size are discarded and redrawn. Math.random() is never used.
entropyChars: Alphabet: {{pool}} characters, length: {{length}} → {{length}} × log₂({{pool}}) ≈ {{bits}} bits. That is how many attempts an attacker who knows the method would need to try them all.
entropyWords: Word list: {{pool}} words → word count × log₂({{pool}}) ≈ {{bits}} bits (extras such as digits are added exactly).
constrainedNote: Active extra rules (minimums, class requirement, no repeats) slightly reduce the real entropy – the formula is then a mild upper bound.
zxcvbnBody: zxcvbn searches for dictionary hits, keyboard patterns, repeats and dates. Result: score {{score}} of 4, estimated guesses 10^{{guesses}}.
scenariosTitle: Crack time in four attack scenarios
privacyBody: Nothing. Generation, analysis and the QR code all run locally. The only exception: the optional leak check (opt-in in the settings) sends the first 5 characters of the locally computed SHA-1 hash – never the password itself.
